title: Every Primitive Invocation ends in an Artifact Edit Proposal, so operating requires amending the Agent's own constitution
content:
Each Instance Configuration Document in Obex's Artifact closes with a **Data Repository** containing exactly three branches, in the same order every time: **Initial Planning**, **Operational GovOps Review**, and **Artifact Edit Proposal** (A.6.1.1.5.2.1.1.3.1.3.x for Agent Creation, and identically at A.6.1.1.5.2.1.2.3.1.3.x, A.6.1.1.5.2.1.4.2.1.3.x and A.6.1.1.5.2.2.1.2.1.3.x).

Read as a process rather than as storage, this is the Invocation lifecycle: someone plans the Invocation, Operational GovOps reviews it, and the result is proposed as an edit to the Artifact. The repository is the evidence trail for each stage.

The third stage is the load-bearing one. An Invocation is not complete when capital moves or a contract deploys — it is complete when the Agent's governing document is amended to record it. Doing anything materially new therefore requires changing the text that governs you, which forces every operational act through the same amendment scrutiny as a rule change.

That is an unusual and demanding design. It guarantees the Artifact is a live and complete description of the Agent rather than a stale charter, which is what makes tree-position-as-status meaningful elsewhere in the document. The cost is process weight on every action, and a standing incentive to characterise activity as falling under an existing Instance rather than requiring a new Invocation.
description: The Data Repository of every Instance Configuration Document has the same three branches — Initial Planning, Operational GovOps Review, Artifact Edit Proposal
